title: Review of c03's FCH gated micelles: SIBWD replicates on seed 17; gate ablation removes the contrast, but a 100x uniformly lowered cargo D also holds >= 2x to t=400
summary: Fresh labkit re-run on seed 17 (T=400): ~30 micelles from white noise, 24 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges; the shell q forms a ring on 242/248 individuals (rim/core 9.86, rim/outside 4.98) and 99.4% of body-frames hold the cargo at >= 2x the outside (27x aggregate at t=400). Gate off (beta=0, seed 17): 1.1x, 0% of bodies >= 2x at the end. Lowered-D twins without the gate: Dc=0.1 (the world's bulk D, exp(-8q) ~ 0.06-0.2 in core and medium) gives 1.8x at t=400 and 43% of bodies >= 2x; Dc=0.01 gives 99.9% of body-frames >= 2x to t=400 (9.3x), decaying to 2.0x at t=1200 (77% of bodies), against the gated world's 6.0x (95%) at t=1200 on the same bodies (identical u dynamics, 69 persistent splits, gen 5). The ring is a real barrier (cargo D at the ring 1e-5 to 1e-12), but a uniformly 100x slower cargo mimics the containment at the claim's horizon.

verdicts.limitation: Not beyond diffusion at the claim's horizon: with the gate removed and the cargo diffusivity lowered 100x everywhere, 99.9% of body-frames still hold >= 2x to t=400; the gate's advantage is quantitative (about 3x higher contrast at every time, 6.0x vs 2.0x at t=1200) and a bulk-matched D (0.1) does fail (1.8x). Both arms decline after t~400 as the domain crowds and cargo leaked at fission necks pools between bodies. Shell and cargo are passive (division is identical with and without the gate). One fresh seed; resolution not re-tested.
